target_customer: Individuals and teams in sales, customer success and operations who record video meetings; paid tiers for teams
problem: People lose the substance of meetings and spend time taking notes. Fathom records, transcribes and summarizes calls, with a generous free tier.
business_model: Freemium SaaS with paid per-seat team plans

founders.name: Richard White
previous_startups: UserVoice (founder, later led for many years)
founders.background_notes: Worked with Justin Kan and Emmett Shear at Kiko, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on third-party speech and language models rather than proprietary models; the work was integrations, UX and reliable capture across Zoom, Meet and Teams.

defensibility.rationale: Many notetakers (Otter, Fireflies, tl;dv, Read.ai) emerged; edge was free tier and UX, plus meeting history lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms added native summaries, but Fathom kept growing and sold to Superhuman in September 2026.

market_need_then: Zoom fatigue and the pandemic meeting load in 2020 and 2021 created demand for call recording and summaries; Fathom launched on Product Hunt on Dec 8, 2021 and was a Zoom marketplace launch partner.

identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, playful and punchy ('AI notetaking that is out of this world', 'Stop guessing. Ask Fathom.')

branding.brand_signature: Free-forever unlimited recording, which the CEO said was an early vision

rebrands.why: Not stated; domain moved as the product became an AI notetaker

branding.community_and_virality: Crowdfunded 2 million dollars of the Series A from its own users on Wefunder; reports of 500K plus companies using it.

brand_strength.rationale: A free tier and user crowdfunding show real affection, though the name is shared with unrelated Fathom companies and press on the brand itself was not found.

outcome_analysis: Fathom launched a free AI notetaker for Zoom in 2021 and grew through a generous free tier and Zoom marketplace distribution, raising 4.7 million dollars in 2022 and 17 million in September 2024, including 2 million crowdfunded from users. It reportedly reached more than 400,000 monthly users and was bought by Superhuman on September 14, 2026 for undisclosed terms as notetakers consolidated into productivity suites.
notes: Seed amount: YC page headline says 4.7M but the TechCrunch URL slug says 3.7M; 4.7M used since the Series A press coverage also says 4.7M. Total raised varies (21.8M to over 30M) across sources; valuation figures (73M Latka, 94M PitchBook) are unverified and not recorded. Zoom investment mentioned on YC page (Aug 2021 Zoom fund news) but not confirmed. Competition empty: search returned only current comparison pages for Otter, Fireflies, Gong, tl;dv, none dated near Dec 2021.
